Criterion: Verify that electrical power is supplied to all safety critical engine systems under all flight conditions. Standard: The engine driven alternator/generator is adequately sized to provide safe and reliable electrical power at all specified engine speeds. Seamless transition to and from back-up power is supplied by the air vehicle for all engine safety critical systems and components. Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis, test and review of documentation. Analysis of the engine's total power consumption establishes the power required to be generated by the alternator, generator and air vehicle. Analysis, bench and engine testing demonstrate the ability to meet the electrical power generation requirements of the engine specification, when not installed in the air vehicle. Flight testing demonstrates the engine's ability to meet the electrical power generation requirements of the engine specification, when installed in the air vehicle. Analysis and test of the air vehicle's power generation and battery systems demonstrate their ability to meet the back-up power requirements of the engine specification. References: JSSG-2007: A.3.7.4.1 - A.3.7.4.2, A.4.7.4.1 - A.4.7.4.2 14 CFR 33.28

Standard: The engine driven alternator and generator is sized to provide uninterruptible electrical power where the engine is the primary or alternate power source for the engine control system, engine ignition system, and any other engine electrical accessory. Transfer between primary and alternate power sources does not interrupt engine operation. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Review documentation (e.g., hardware drawings, system configuration descriptions, design data records, inspection reports, or other substantiating records, reports, ICD) and verify design of the engine driven alternator and generator. Analysis.
  (1) Analysis of the engine's electrical consumption establishes the power generated by the primary or alternate power source. Demonstration.
    (1) Demonstrate during ground testing, the transfer between primary and alternate power sources does not interrupt engine operation. Test.
      (1) Lab test: Bench testing verifies the electrical power generation.
      (2) Lab test: Engine ground-based sea level and altitude cell testing verifies the electrical power generation. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
    (2) Demonstrate during flight testing, the transfer between primary and alternate power sources does not interrupt engine operation. Test.
    (3) Flight test: Flight testing verifies the electrical power generation.
